title: X Feed Digest
summary: OpenAI shipped major platform upgrades: GPT‑5.3‑Codex for all developers, broader file ingestion in the Responses API, and gpt‑realtime‑1.5 for voice apps.
Claude/Anthropic updates emphasize tooling governance: Claude Code 2.1.53 changes tool orchestration and Anthropic released Responsible Scaling Policy v3.
AI funding stayed hot with big rounds for MatX ($500M AI chips) and Wayve ($1.8B autonomy), plus a free compressed model from Multiverse Computing.
Fintech and policy headlines centered on Stripe (PayPal acquisition talks + valuation jump) and post‑tariff refund uncertainty, with cyber/geopolitics adding risk signals.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: GPT‑5.3‑Codex in Responses API
items.body: GPT‑5.3‑Codex is now available to all developers via the Responses API, expanding access to OpenAI’s coding‑focused model for agent and app builds.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Responses API file inputs expanded
items.body: Responses API now accepts common office formats (docx, pptx, csv, xlsx, and more), allowing agents to ingest real‑world documents without manual conversion.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: gpt‑realtime‑1.5 for voice apps
items.body: The Realtime API gained gpt‑realtime‑1.5 with improved instruction‑following, tool calling, and multilingual accuracy for voice workflows.

items.title: @ClaudeCodeLog: Claude Code 2.1.53
items.body: Claude Code 2.1.53 prioritizes dedicated tools for orchestration and removes the built‑in Bash runner; new system rules add permissions, tagging, and output compression.

items.title: @AnthropicAI: Responsible Scaling Policy v3
items.body: Anthropic published version 3 of its Responsible Scaling Policy, aiming for stronger transparency and refined safeguards as model capabilities scale.

items.title: @TechCrunch: MatX raises $500M for AI chips
items.body: AI‑chip startup MatX raised $500M to build Nvidia‑challenging hardware, underscoring investor appetite for alternative AI compute.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Wayve closes $1.8B round
items.body: Autonomous‑driving startup Wayve secured a $1.8B round backed by Nvidia, Uber, and automakers, one of the largest recent AV raises.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Multiverse releases free compressed model
items.body: Multiverse Computing launched a free compressed AI model, highlighting continued pushes toward efficient inference and lower compute cost.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Opal gets automated workflows
items.body: Google added automated workflow creation to Opal, its no‑code AI workflow builder, expanding automation options for visual pipelines.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Stripe eyes PayPal deal
items.body: TechCrunch reports Stripe is exploring a deal to buy some or all of PayPal, a potential reshaping of the payments landscape if talks progress.

items.title: @TechCrunch: Stripe valuation jumps to $159B
items.body: Stripe’s valuation reportedly surged 74% to $159B, marking a major private‑market repricing for the fintech leader.

items.title: @TheEconomist: Tariff refunds could be messy
items.body: After the Supreme Court struck down some Trump‑era tariffs, businesses want refunds, but The Economist notes the claims process will be slow and politically fraught.

items.title: @TechCrunch: U.S. sanctions Russian zero‑day broker
items.body: The Treasury sanctioned a Russian zero‑day broker accused of buying stolen exploits from a U.S. defense contractor, escalating cyber enforcement pressure.

items.title: @_The_Prophet__: Iran escalation choreography
items.body: A Reuters‑sourced thread argues Trump will use the State of the Union to build a public case on Iran, framing it as escalation signaling that could ripple into oil and risk assets.

items.title: @_philschmid: How to write AGENTS.md
items.body: Research‑backed guidance says AGENTS.md files should be short and human‑written; auto‑generated or overly detailed context hurts success rates and cost. It recommends focusing on WHAT/WHY/HOW and linking out for details.

items.title: @sc102704: Prediction markets are underused
items.body: Prediction markets processed $44B last year with strong calibration, but the post argues businesses still ignore them. The opportunity is tooling that makes market probabilities decision‑ready.

items.title: @RayDalio: Investing in the Big Cycle
items.body: Ray Dalio shared a new chapter on “Investing in Light of the Big Cycle,” outlining how to position portfolios amid shifting geopolitical order.
